standard.title: Medical Textiles — Shoe Covers — Specification
standard.sector: Textiles / Technical Textiles for Medtech Applications

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Medtech Applications Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements, design, and testing parameters for disposable and reusable shoe covers intended to be used for medical purposes during various procedures to protect patients and materials from the transfer of microorganisms, particulates, and other contaminants. It explicitly excludes the requirements of legging or boot legging used in operating theatres.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Medical Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all shoe covers manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 17349 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified medical shoe covers is a criminal offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. MSMEs are granted phased transition timelines, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to medical shoe covers.
requirements: Every commercial pack of shoe covers must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to verify conformity.
Shoe covers must be provided with an elastic strip or other suitable fastening mechanism at the opening to cover the foot and shoe properly. They must be slip-resistant and water-resistant.
May be supplied in non-sterile or sterilized condition as per the buyer's requirement. If sterile, the packaging must maintain product integrity throughout its shelf life.
Manufacture and preparation must be conducted under proper hygienic conditions. The shoe covers must be clean and free from substances liable to cause tendering during storage.
The total viable microbial bioburden must not exceed 300 CFU/100 cm² when tested in accordance with ISO 11737-1.
The tensile strength must exceed 20 N when tested per IS 15891 (Part 3) for non-wovens or IS 1969 (Part 1) for wovens.
The bursting strength must exceed 40 kPa when tested in accordance with hydraulic methods of IS 1966 (Part 1).
A lot comprises all shoe covers of the same material and dimensions produced under similar conditions of manufacture and sterilization. Random samples must be selected per IS 4905.
